title: Calculate DNA Sequence Edit Distance
real_world_story: A genetics research system compares two DNA samples and needs to determine how many basic changes are required to transform one DNA sequence into another.

real_world_connection.input_represents: Two DNA sequences obtained from biological samples
real_world_connection.target_represents: The minimum number of changes required between the two sequences
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Computing the minimum number of insertions, deletions, and substitutions required to transform one DNA sequence into another

problem_statement: Given two DNA sequences, calculate the minimum number of operations required to transform the first sequence into the second. The allowed operations are insertion, deletion, and substitution of a nucleotide, and each operation has a cost of 1.
task: Determine the minimum number of nucleotide-level edits required to transform the first DNA sequence into the second.
input_format: The first line contains the first DNA sequence. The second line contains the second DNA sequence.
output_format: Print a single integer representing the minimum edit distance between the two DNA sequences.
constraints: DNA sequences contain only the characters A, C, G, and T

examples.explanation: Four nucleotide-level operations are required to transform the first sequence into the second.
Only one nucleotide substitution is required to transform the first sequence into the second.

expected_algorithm.name: Edit Distance using Dynamic Programming
expected_algorithm.reason: Each position in the DNA sequences can be handled through insertion, deletion, or substitution while previously computed results avoid repeated calculations.

hint: Create a table for prefixes of both DNA sequences.
If the current nucleotides are equal, no additional operation is required.
If they differ, consider insertion, deletion, and substitution and choose the minimum.
real_world_takeaway: Edit distance can help researchers quantify differences between DNA sequences and study how closely two biological samples are related at the sequence level.
